summary: Introductory hosted-API demo covering chat/text generation basics: streaming responses, model parameters (temperature, max_tokens, top_p), retry behavior, and simple cost/latency tradeoffs. Customer is evaluating for a POC to replace an in-house inference service; concerns around latency, data retention, and SOC2. Agreed to run pilot benchmarks with sample prompts.
meeting_header:
Date: 2026-03-24
Time: 16:00 - 16:48 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Laura Chen (Redwood AE), Miguel Santos (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (CTO, Crescent Fintech), Mark Davis (Lead ML Engineer), Sara Liu (PM)
transcript:
[00:00] Laura Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Laura with Redwood Inference, AE for your account. Miguel will do the technical walkthrough.
[00:08] Priya Shah: Hi Laura, thanks. We have about 45 minutes. Looking forward to getting a feel for the hosted API and how streaming works.
[00:15] Miguel Santos: Great thanks Priya. Quick agenda: quick intro, live demo of chat + text gen, show streaming, go over params (temp, top_p, max_tokens), retries and idempotency, and then Q&A. Sound good?
[00:27] Mark Davis: Yep sounds good. We're currently running our own in‑house service on k8s with a KV cahce and some custom batching. Latency is okay but cost is high and scaling is painful.
[00:37] Miguel Santos: Got it, thanks. A lot of customers start there. I'll share screen — demo deck and then a quick Postman/CLI call.
[00:45] Miguel Santos: (screen share) So first: simple chat generate call to hosted API. We call /v1/chat/completions, pass messages, and we can optionally stream tokens back with chunked responses.
[01:10] Miguel Santos: Example code: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions -d '{"model":"rwd-1-chat","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize the attached notes."}], "stream":true, "temperature":0.2 }' 
[01:30] Sara Liu: When you say stream, do you mean server-sent events? How do we handle partial tokens in our UI?
[01:38] Miguel Santos: Yes, we use streaming with chunked JSON events. Each event contains token text and a delta. You can render progressively; we also include finalization event. For partial tokens we provide a 'role' and 'delta' pieces — typical SSE pattern.
[01:58] Priya Shah: Any caveats with streaming and long responses? We sometimes hit > 1k tokens.
[02:05] Miguel Santos: We support large sequences; the runtime does incremental KV cache management. For very long outputs we recommend enabling incremental flushes and possibly lower batch sizes to keep tail latency predictable. Also note cost grows with output tokens.
[02:28] Mark Davis: How do we control hallucination vs verbosity?
[02:32] Miguel Santos: Two levers: temperature and top_p primarily. Temperature 0 for deterministic, 0.7 for more creative. top_p can also limit sampling mass. We showed examples in the deck: same prompt with temp 0.0 vs 0.7. Also you can set max_tokens to hard bound length.
[02:55] Laura Chen: Quick product point — our Console lets you run A/B comparisons across parameters and see token counts and latency per call which helps pick the sweet spot for cost/quality.
[03:12] Sara Liu: Nice. Does the Console show per-route latency percentiles?
[03:16] Miguel Santos: Yes P50/95/99 and token breakdown, plus per-model dashboards.
[03:23] Priya Shah: Ok about retries — we need to know best practice. Our infra sometimes gets 5xx and retries cause duplicate charges or duplicate side effects.
[03:32] Miguel Santos: Good question. For idempotency: include an idempotency_key in the header for non-idempotent operations or for any request where you want at-most-once semantics. Our server will dedupe within a short window. For streaming endpoints you get partials — we recommend client logic to detect terminal events. Retries on 5xx are fine with exponential backoff; for 429s we also return Retry-After.
[03:58] Mark Davis: How long do you keep logs and request content? We have strict retention rules.
[04:05] Laura Chen: For hosted API, default retention is 30 days; enterprise plans can extend or opt out of retention entirely. We have SOC 2 Type II, and offer KMS integration for keys; audit logs are available in Redwood Console.
[04:22] Priya Shah: Is it possible to disable retention completely for PII workflows?
[04:27] Miguel Santos: Yes, on our Dedicated/Private deployments you can opt to not persist payloads, or we can configure hosted enterprise accounts to route logs to your KMS/encrypted blob store and short retention. We'll follow up with the security doc.
[04:40] Sara Liu: You mentioned batching. How does automatic batching work with streaming?
[04:46] Miguel Santos: Batching is mostly for backend throughput. Streaming still sends incremental events; batching groups similar requests in the serving runtime to optimize kernel usage. We expose batching and latency SLO tunables at the deployment level. For chat low-latency paths we use continuous batching to keep per-request latency low.
[05:10] Laura Chen: Real quick — any questions about pricing? We bill per input + output token. There's also reserved capacity options if you need predictable throughput.
[05:18] Priya Shah: Our cost model needs to be under X per 1k queries; we'll need a rough calc.
[05:22] Laura Chen: We'll send a pricing sheet with typical token profiles and a calc for text summarization workloads.
[05:28] Miguel Santos: Back to demo: show param changes — temperature 0.0, max_tokens 120, top_p 0.95. Live call: streaming enabled.
[05:40] [demo plays back streaming response]
[06:10] Mark Davis: That looks good. Latency seems fine. What's typical p95 for small chat (100 tokens)?
[06:16] Miguel Santos: For our hosted rwd-1-chat on standard region it's ~120-180ms p95 for 100-token runs on typical load. Dedicated GPU pools get lower and more consistent.
[06:30] Priya Shah: Are there regional differences? Our EU customers need EU data residency.
[06:35] Laura Chen: Yes we have region pins; you can route by region and we also offer private deployment in EU for residency requirements.
[06:44] Sara Liu: Can we customize model quantization or request a specific model variant?
[06:49] Miguel Santos: Model catalog supports curated variants. We recommend a quantized variant for cost reduction; Redwood Optimize will suggest quantization profiles based on your workload. For hosted we surface recommended variants and fallback policies.
[07:05] Mark Davis: For retries again, if streaming was interrupted mid-response and we retry, will the second call resume?
[07:13] Miguel Santos: We don't offer resumable streams out-of-the-box today. Best practice: client detects interruption and retries the whole request with the same idempotency key; server dedupe prevents double side effects, but you'll likely re-render the response from scratch. For long-form resumable support that's a roadmap item.
[07:33] Priya Shah: Any gotchas with rate limits? Our traffic is bursty.
[07:37] Laura Chen: We have tiered rate limits with burst buckets and per-account quota. For bursty workloads, Dedicated with burst capacity or autoscaling policies works well. Also consider local caching of prompt prefixes to reduce token usage.
[07:53] Miguel Santos: Quick live example of changing temperature inline — show how the same prompt yields more conservative vs creative output.
[08:05] [demo examples]
[08:30] Sara Liu: Can the Console simulate costs for different param combos?
[08:33] Miguel Santos: Yes, Console can run a quick simulation over a prompt set and show expected token counts and cost across models/variants.
[08:40] Priya Shah: Security again: SSO and RBAC? We need team-level controls.
[08:44] Laura Chen: We support SSO (SAML/OIDC), RBAC with role granularity, and audit logs. We'll send the security pack with SOC2 and ISO certs.
[08:54] Mark Davis: For the POC we want to test throughput and p95 with our real prompts. Can Redwood run benchmarks?
[08:59] Miguel Santos: Yes, we can run a pilot benchmark on hosted or Dedicated. Typical pilot: you provide a prompt set, we run a battery for 24-48 hours and produce latency, cost, and quality metrics. We'll share the benchmark script after the call.
[09:18] Priya Shah: Timeline wise, we want to decide in two weeks. Our stakeholders: procurement and security will need the docs.
[09:25] Laura Chen: Noted. We'll send pricing, security pack, and benchmark plan.
[09:30] [short silence, demo continues with example retries]
[09:45] Miguel Santos: Now about retries: show sample code. header: Idempotency-Key: <uuid>. Backoff: start 300ms, then 600ms, 1.2s. On 429 consider jitter. We also return Retry-After header.
[10:02] Mark Davis: Good. Do you have SDK helpers?
[10:06] Miguel Santos: Yes official SDKs (JS/Python/Go) include retry helpers and streaming clients. The JS SDK has a stream iterator that yields chunks.
[10:16] Sara Liu: Are there any billing surprises with retries? Like if we retry twice and both succeed, are we billed twice?
[10:22] Laura Chen: We bill for tokens processed. If the first attempt was fully processed and then second processed, you'll be billed twice. That's why idempotency dedupe and retry windows help avoid double processing. For streaming interruptions where server didn't complete, typically only one attempt incurs cost. We can go over edge cases in the security pack.
[10:43] [Demo: show Console dashboard - per-route latency, token counts]
[11:05] Priya Shah: Ok let's talk about model versioning: we need stable rollouts.
[11:10] Miguel Santos: We support pinning model versions and rollout policies (canary, A/B). You can configure automatic fallback to a smaller variant if larger model is unavailable. Console shows rollouts and tracing per request.
[11:25] Mark Davis: Do you surface token-level cost in traces? We need to tie requests to cost centers.
[11:29] Laura Chen: Yes per-request token breakdown and cost attribution by route and token.
[11:36] Sara Liu: For data residency again, can logs be shipped to our S3?
[11:40] Miguel Santos: Yes we can integrate with a customer blob store or forward logs via secure transfer; for dedicated/private deployments it's straightforward.
[11:50] Priya Shah: Any enterprise SLA for hosted API?
[11:54] Laura Chen: Enterprise plans include SLA options for uptime and latency targets; Dedicated has stronger SLOs. We'll include SLA terms in the contract.
[12:05] [fast-forward demo: showing streaming latency and parameter UI in Console]
[18:30] Miguel Santos: Quick Q&A recap — streaming is SSE-like, params control quality/cost, use idempotency for retries, Console assists with cost/latency tuning, security pack will address retention and SSO.
[18:45] Priya Shah: Sounds good. A few technical follow-ups: can we get the exact p95 numbers for our region, and a benchmark with our 2000 prompts?
[18:54] Miguel Santos: Yes we'll run a pilot; Miguel to own benchmark script.
[19:00] Laura Chen: I'll send pricing and next steps.
[19:05] Priya Shah: For the pilot, can we get a test API key with limited quota?
[19:09] Laura Chen: Yes, we'll provision a trial key scoped to the pilot.
[19:15] Mark Davis: One last question: debugging - is there request-level replay?
[19:20] Miguel Santos: We have traces and you can replay requests internally for debugging with proper auth; we don't provide raw PII replays unless authorized.
[19:32] [End of demo portion, move to closing]
[19:40] Laura Chen: Quick recap and next steps: 1) We'll send pricing and security docs. 2) Miguel will share benchmark script. 3) We provision a trial key. 4) Customer provides prompt set and SLOs.
[19:58] Priya Shah: Great thanks, do that and we'll align procurement.
[20:03] Sara Liu: Thanks everyone.
[20:06] Laura Chen: Thanks all. We'll follow up by EOD with the packet.
[20:12] [Call ends]
